question: Can a small learner trained to correct a real completed portfolio, including its agreements, do better than adding another unconditioned voter? A stand-alone nonlinear head corrected 33 unanimously wrong cases but hurt overall when blended.
model: Infer the deployed member set and actual weights from each ordinary course-development run. Use its earlier common held probabilities as a fixed log-odds offset. Learn a single ridge-penalized logistic correction to that offset from the true earlier labels. Describe a pair by signed differences in ordinary shape/count statistics, their products with the matching symmetric means, and their products with six topic coordinates from word TF-IDF on the fitting texts alone. Use no case IDs, external corpora, topic names or handpicked words. No intercept, preserving sign when sides are swapped. Stay with the baseline when the correction is zero; it may change an agreement as well as a disagreement.
split: Reuse actual row-aligned primary, confirmation_1 and confirmation_2 trials of the selected members from each of the two course-development runs. Require at least two complete folds and one spare fit. Use only these held rows to learn the vocabulary, topic projection, scales and correction, with penalty sqrt(number of rows). Freeze the complete correction before the two remaining review folds. Enable it only if both avoid losses and their row-weighted accuracy gain reaches +0.20 points. Lock shadow, deployed and original predictions on the anonymous outer feature packet, then read only its training-development answers. Report agreement changes, including any recoveries where all deployed members were wrong. The two previously studied working panels do not constitute new designated validation.
limits: At most one small supervised fit and one unsupervised topic projection per completed run. Zero base-model training or API. Advance only on positive deployed net in both disjoint outer panels and +0.20 points pooled. No designated 940 labels, official test or H2.
